PRODUCTION COMPLETE — all 11 artifacts written to the working directory, from sampled stochastic dynamics only. Full run 33 s; two independent invocations of `python simulation.py` produce byte-identical .npy/.json artifacts (md5-verified), so the pipeline is deterministic.

WHAT WAS RUN (your rulings honored exactly)
- Step semantics: n_steps_per_T = 57505 were ALL used as production steps; **11501 extra thermalisation steps (20%) in ADDITION** per temperature, same kernel/same T, never written to any artifact; checkpoints at s = 0,250,…,57500 → **n_ckpt = 231** (no 25% discard scheme; stated in code comments, in the module docstring and in `warnings`).
- eps = mean(temperature_list) = 0.865400 fixed before the ladder and NOT retuned afterwards (the mean is 0.8654, not the 0.8757 I quoted in the plan — arithmetic slip in the plan only; the code always used the file's actual mean).
- Q = (1/M)·Σ 1{r_ij < 1.10·r0_ij}, clipped to [0,1], identical at every T, and used unchanged for `native_contact_probability.npy` and the Jaccard adjacency.
- T_star from interpolated <Q>(T)=0.5; the C_v curve is a reported diagnostic only.
- Two analysis hardenings during the run (physics untouched): (i) the fine C_v originally came from a pooled WHAM p(E), whose sparse tails produced a spurious 107 spike (direct values are 12–18), so it is now single-histogram Ferenc–Neville reweighting of the *raw* energy trajectory of the **nearest** ladder temperature, minimum reweighting effective sample size 175/231; (ii) the naive mode finder reported 5 "modes" from shot noise and a 1.69 kBT barrier, so mode acceptance now requires prominence ≥ max(15% of the smoothed maximum, 2 shot-noise σ of the smoothed density) and basin mass ≥ 10%; with that, the landscape is single-mode and barrier/separation are reported as 0.

Ladder bracketing: <Q>(T_min)=0.6649, <Q>(T_max)=0.4602 → 0.5 IS bracketed (segment k=2, T=0.795740…0.935060), T_star well inside the interval (not at an edge), so rule 3(c) was not needed.

T_star = **0.9163786**, method: piecewise-linear interpolation on the bracketing segment (PCHIP was auto-disabled because <Q>(T) is not strictly monotone — it rises 0.4396→0.4602 between the top two rungs; recorded in `warnings`). Dedicated full-budget run at exactly T_star (same protocol, seed rule): <Q> = **0.5433**, var 0.00978, lag1 0.525, n_eff ≈ 72 → SE(<Q>) ≈ 0.012, i.e. the dedicated run lands 0.043 above the 0.5 target — that offset is the finite-sampling scatter of <Q>(T), reported in `warnings`.

FREE ENERGY AT T_star (dedicated run, 50 bins on [0,1], F = -kBT·ln[P/Pmax], min exactly 0)
- Modes found: **1** at Q = 0.53, basin mass 1.00. Smoothing σ = 1.0 bin; acceptance threshold 0.0753 (max of 15% of the smoothed maximum 0.0988 and 2 shot-noise σ). Raw candidate prominences were [0.036, 0.097, 0.062, 0.031, 0.019] — only one exceeds the threshold, and only marginally, so **mode_separation = 0** and **free_energy_barrier_kT = 0** (no barrier inferred from a shoulder, as instructed).
- Histogram mass: bottom 10 bins (Q<0.2) = **0.0000**, top 10 bins (Q≥0.8) = **0.0087**. F(Q) ≈ 0.92 kBT* at Q=0.40 and 1.20 kBT* at Q=0.70 — a smooth broad single well; any "barrier" from this data would be sampling noise.
- Empty bins are handled with a Jeffreys pseudocount (0.5 counts) so F is finite (max 3.92 kBT*) instead of divergent; documented in `warnings` and not affecting populated bins.

JACCARD AT THE LOWEST TEMPERATURE = 29/66 = **0.439394** (|reference adjacency| = 36, |final adjacency| = 59, both under the identical rule |i-j| ≥ 4 and d < 8.8797). The low-T simulated state is *more compact* than the synthetic reference (Rg 6.342 vs 7.010), which creates 23 extra adjacencies — this is why the union is large; 29 of the 36 reference relations survive (consistent with <Q> = 0.665 at the stricter 1.10·r0 tolerance). final_coords.npy is the last production checkpoint (s = 57500) of the T = 0.517101 run, verified elementwise identical (max|diff| = 0.0).

λ SENSITIVITY (diagnostic only; no artifact uses it): tolerance 1.00·r0 → <Q> ladder = 0.447…0.327 (entirely below 0.5, T* → 0.211 by end-point extrapolation); 1.10·r0 → 0.665…0.460 (brackets, T* = 0.916); 1.20·r0 → 0.819…0.572 (entirely above, T* → 1.417). So the T* estimate moves by ±0.4 in reduced temperature with the tolerance — materially. The pre-registered 1.10·r0 definition was used everywhere.

HEAT CAPACITY: `heat_capacity_curve.npy` is (2,121), row 0 spanning exactly [0.517101, 1.213698] (n_fine = 121, documented choice, no reweighting outside the sampled interval), row 1 strictly finite, range 12.588–19.735, max 19.735 at T = 0.592566 (`peak_heat_capacity`). Direct ladder-point C_v = var(E)/T² is stored unsmoothed in `temperature_observables.json`. Honest reading: var(E) grows monotonically with T (4.8→18.5) and is divided by T², so there is no meaningful interior critical peak — the "raw C_v maximum" is a broad crossover near the cold end, which is exactly why it was not used to define T_star.

SELF-VALIDATION BLOCK (printed by simulation.py before exit, all assertions passing)
- All 11 required names present; shapes/dtype/finite: final_coords (20,3), order_parameter_trajectory (6,231), order_parameter_histograms (6,50), heat_capacity_curve (2,121), transition_free_energy_profile (2,50), q_energy_joint_histograms (6,20,20), native_contact_probability (6,36) — all float64, all finite.
- Histogram rows sum to 1 (max dev 1.1e-16); every joint slice sums to 1 (max dev 2.2e-16); Q trajectory confined to [0.1389, 0.8611] ⊂ [0,1]; free-energy row 1 minimum exactly 0.00000000000000000 and bin centers strictly increasing; contact columns lexicographic in (i,j) ((0,4),(0,5),(1,5),…); native_contact_probability ∈ [0.030, 0.922]; JSON key lists match the spec character-for-character and in order; all JSON scalars finite; PNG signature 1560×1080, colortype 2, IEND present, 55 kB.
- Physics self-checks: U(reference) = -31.1544 = -M·eps exactly and |F(reference)| = 0 (the reference is an exact equilibrium of the pair potential); force vs finite-difference -dU/dr agree to ~1e-7; sampled kinetic temperature matches the set T to 1-2% (an earlier force-accumulator bug — numpy fancy-index `+=` with repeated bead indices — was found in the pilot and replaced by bincount scatter).

RESIDUAL NOISE / LIMITATIONS (stated in `warnings` too; 10 warnings recorded)
- Checkpoints are autocorrelated: lag-1(Q) = 0.47–0.65, so the 231 checkpoints are ~50–82 effective samples per temperature; var(E) and hence C_v (and any barrier) inherit that noise; the 20×20 joint histograms rest on ~50–80 correlated samples (85–98 of 400 cells occupied per temperature), so they are lumpy by construction.
- <Q>(T) is not strictly monotone across the ladder (0.4396 at 1.074 vs 0.4602 at 1.214) — within ~2 SE given n_eff; the T* interpolation therefore uses the lowest-T crossing.
- Interaction strengths are not in the parameter file; k_b = 20, eps = mean(T), well width 0.35·r0_ij, WCA σ = 3.8781 (= min reference non-bonded distance for |i-j|≥4 / 2^(1/6)) are my pre-registered deterministic choices, and T* is model-dependent through them (λ sensitivity above quantifies part of it).
- The reference contact network is over-coordinated (cutoff 8.8797 = 2.3 bond lengths), so the transition is a broad crossover rather than two-phase coexistence; consequently mode_separation and barrier are 0 by rule.
- Excluded volume is applied only to |i-j| ≥ min_seq_separation (standard Gō convention, as approved). Consequence: short-range sequence neighbours can pass close — in final_coords the |i-j| = 3 pair (9,12) reaches 1.571 while the closest contact-eligible (|i-j|≥4) pair stays at 4.652 > σ, so Q and the WCA core are unaffected. If you prefer excluded volume for |i-j| ≥ 2 as well, that is a one-line change plus a re-run (~35 s).
